commit on ddflow/fix-Bb5b8b17161: phrase route (testidents.changed_phrases), bare-import resolution (testreach._bare), GOVERNS on compat test_surface, recall replay widened to 40 merges

chunk_findings.detail: `changed_phrases` spawns git subprocesses per changed `.py` file: up to two `_diff` calls (`base...tip` and, when `tip == "HEAD"`, `HEAD`) plus one `W.git(..., "ls-files", ...)` per iteration. The intent says the recall replay was widened to 40 merges; a merge touching N `.py` files therefore costs ~3·N git processes. For a merge touching 200 Python files that is ~600 process spawns per merge and ~24 000 across 40 merges, each git call reading the index/repo, so `changed_phrases` alone can turn selection from sub-second into minutes. Nothing bounds `files` and no single `git diff base...tip -- <files>` is reused, so a large refactor merge (e.g. a rename/reformat sweep touching most of `ddflow/`) is the input that makes the new route pathologically slow.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testidents.py `changed_phrases`

chunk_findings.detail: The diff-line filter drops any content line whose text begins with `--` or `++`, mistaking it for the `--- a/...` / `+++ b/...` file headers. A source line such as a SQL comment inside a triple-quoted literal (`-- fetch rows`), an ASCII-art banner inside a string, or a removed line that is literally `--` becomes `--- fetch rows` after the leading `-` is added, matches `ln[:3] == "---"`, and is silently discarded. The phrase extracted from that literal never enters `phrases`, so a test that asserts on the reworded/removed message is no longer selected — exactly the recall miss this change is meant to close, reproduced whenever a changed/lost string literal contains a line starting with `--` or `++`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testidents.py `changed_phrases` (the `ln[:3] not in ("---", "+++")` filter)

chunk_findings.detail: `_bare` is consulted for *every* import name that `resolve` cannot match, with no check that the name is actually meant to be a local module. It returns any same-stem `.py` found in a non-package ancestor directory, so external (stdlib/third-party) imports get false edges whenever a helper file happens to share the name. Concrete input: a repo whose `tests/` has no `__init__.py` and contains a fake `tests/queue.py`, plus `tests/test_worker.py` that does `import queue` for the stdlib module. `resolve("queue", g.names)` returns `""` (the file's module name is `tests.queue`), so `_bare("queue", "tests/test_worker.py", homes)` returns `tests.queue`, and the graph gains the edge `tests/test_worker.py -> tests.queue`. Changing the fake helper now selects `test_worker.py`, which never imports it — exactly the "noisy" over-selection this selector is supposed to avoid (`import mock`, `import select`, `import typing`, `import types`, … collide the same way). Over-selection of unrelated tests also inflates every gate run that touches such a helper. There is no allowlist/verification that the bare name is not a resolvable external module (e.g. via `importlib.util.find_spec`), so the new route can only add false positive edges.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testreach.py:96 (`_bare`) / :86 (`_bare_homes`)

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds a selection route based on matching words of string literals gained/lost in a source diff (`TI.changed_phrases` → `TI.phrase_tests`). Per [D-gap-affected-tests-no-partial] the affected-tests gap is explicitly scoped to the import-graph closure ("B-gap-affected-tests builds the import-graph closure only"); lexical string-literal matching is not part of that closure, so this widens the affected-tests criterion beyond the recorded decision. Demonstration: changing one line from `encoding="utf-8"` to `encoding="UTF-8"` in a source file yields a phrase (`utf-8`) that appears in most test files; the selector then pulls those tests in through a non-import-graph route, which is a criterion the decision says this gap must not use.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testselect.py:252 (`pick.many(TI.phrase_tests(...))`, new phrase route) [D-gap-affected-tests-no-partial]

chunk_findings.detail:
The change deletes `MERGES = 4` and collapses the two separate quantities into a single `SCAN = 40`, which the new comment calls "merges replayed (those with both source and tests in them)" while the docstring still says the test "Replays the last SCAN merges of THIS repository". These were previously *different* numbers, and the removed comment records why: with a scan window of `SCAN = 40`, exactly `MERGES = 4` merges had both source and tests and were actually replayed. So the single constant cannot mean both things at once, and either reading is wrong:
- If the loop still iterates the last `SCAN` merges and keeps the ones that have both source and tests (which is what the docstring "the last SCAN merges … (those with both source and tests in them)" says), then the replay count is again only a handful (~4), not 40 — exactly the "four were too few" failure the changelog claims to fix — while `ABSOLUTE_FLOOR` is raised from 0.7 to 0.85 on that same tiny sample.
- If the loop instead scans until 40 qualifying merges are found, then the docstring's "Bounded (`SCAN` merges, a few processes, no network)" guarantee is false: the scan is bounded by the repository's history length, not by `SCAN`, so on a repo with few qualifying merges the replay can walk the whole log.

Demonstrating input: the merge history the old comment describes (40 consecutive merges of which only 4 touch both source and tests) — under the first reading the new test replays 4 merges with a stricter floor, under the second it is not bounded by `SCAN` merges at all.
